name: Quest Protein Bar — Oatmeal Chocolate Chip

source.author: Quest Nutrition
source.notes: Requested via iHerb (il.iherb.com), which is egress-blocked by the network proxy — same iHerb block the codebase already notes. Values taken from Quest's published nutrition panel via web search (manufacturer source). Verify against the physical IL/EU wrapper if that formula differs slightly from the US label.

ingredients.item: protein blend (milk protein isolate, whey protein isolate)
cocoa butter, sea salt, natural flavors, cinnamon, lecithin (sunflower/soy)

steps: Packaged protein bar — eat as-is. Portable snack / on-the-go protein + fiber.

him.verdict: Just about the ideal cut snack. 20 g protein for 180 kcal (~11 g protein per 100 kcal) AND 14 g fiber — nearly half your 32 g/day target in one bar — with just 1 g sugar and ~5 g net carb. High protein + high fiber = strong satiety on a deficit, and it's portable. This is the fiber the protein puffs lacked, so the two complement each other well. Minor notes only: it's ultra-processed and leans on sugar alcohols (erythritol/glycerin) + sucralose/stevia — fine for most, but the sugar alcohols can cause bloating/GI if you eat more than one.
suggested_mods: Best used to rescue a low-protein OR low-fiber day — it fixes both at once
Cap at 1 bar most days; sugar alcohols (5 g) can bloat if you stack them
Pair the two rotation snacks by purpose: puffs for pure protein, this bar when you also need fiber

her_preconception.verdict: A good high-protein, high-fiber snack for her too — 20 g protein and 14 g fiber (fiber genuinely helps pregnancy-related constipation), with almost no sugar. Not a prenatal micronutrient contributor (no meaningful folate/iron/choline). Sweeteners (sucralose, stevia) and erythritol are generally regarded as safe in pregnancy in normal amounts; some prefer to moderate. Contains milk, almond, and soy lecithin — note if relevant to her.
prenatal_highlights: 14 g fiber — helpful for pregnancy constipation

safety_advisories.note: Contains sucralose + stevia + erythritol. Considered safe in pregnancy in normal amounts per FDA; moderate if she prefers to limit non-nutritive sweeteners.
safety_advisories.swap: whole-food protein/fiber snack if she'd rather avoid sweeteners

suggested_mods: Fine as an occasional protein/fiber top-up; pair with fruit for prenatal micros
Allergens: milk, almond (tree nut), soy lecithin

adopted_note: Adopted into the rotation 2026-08-09 as a fixed portable protein+fiber snack (per user request). Label values, so reuse directly: 1 bar (60 g) = 180 kcal, 20 g protein, 14 g fiber, ~5 g net carb. Standing guidance: ~1 bar/day (sugar alcohols can bloat if stacked); use it on days that are short on protein OR fiber.
